name: Caves of Maresha and Bet-Guvrin in the Judean Lowlands as a Microcosm of the Land of the Caves
description: Beneath the rolling hills of Israel's Judean foothills lie about 3,500 hand-carved chambers, dug into soft white chalk under the ancient towns of Maresha and Bet Guvrin. Over some 2,000 years, from the 8th century BCE to the Crusader era, people turned them into cisterns, olive presses, stables, dovecotes, baths, tombs and hideouts. Some of the largest halls rise in vaulted arches held up by sturdy pillars.
